pr_body:
## Summary

We had a guard in the resolve to avoid "self-dependencies" (as in `gps3==0.33.3`), but this guard was _unintentionally_ filtering out recursive extras.

Closes https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/1342.

## Test Plan

Taken from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/1352.
pr_comments: Are these warnings only visible with `-v` — is that why we weren't seeing them?

issue_context.title: `uv pip install "apache-airflow[all]"` fails to install the required extras
issue_context.body:
Hi all, just found out about this project, I've done a lot of work to test and improve real world resolution performance for Pip and done a lot of testing against [Rip](https://github.com/prefix-dev/rip).

I'm very excited to also test `uv`, especially with it's very interesting resolution options!

My first most common test to check any new resolution library is to try `apache-airflow[all]`, when I run (on Linux CPython 3.10):

```
pip install "apache-airflow[all]"
```

I get 428 packages installed, but when I run:

```
uv pip install "apache-airflow[all]"
```

I get 139 packages installed, is uv currently ignoring extras?
comments: It shouldn't be, no! Extras are definitely supported and we have a bunch of test coverage for it. Lemme look into this.

Thanks for the report! It looks like you found a hole in our test scenarios.

I've reproduced this in https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/1352

We don't support recursive extras at this time, but will asap!

review_comments: Thanks! This file is actually generated. If you want to fix it, it's sourced from https://github.com/zanieb/packse/blob/main/scenarios/extras.json
I just renamed and re-ordered these (especially since `extra` got shadowed below).
